incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: latency_alert p99 > 2.0s for coda-prod-1 (single-tenant customer 'Coda')
ryan: Oncall here. I'm looking at traces. p95 ~ 450ms, p99 ~ 2.6s across the fleet but concentrated on nodes serving coda-prod-1.
Anya: see grafana -> https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency?panel=tail&cluster=coda-prod-1
Miguel: streaming stalls observed. logs show repeated 'kv cache miss' spikes and very long prefix lengths from client prompts.
EngRuntime: stack traces show worker backlog and scheduling preemption. Sequence length distribution skewed to 6k-10k tokens for many requests.
Lina: customer reported increased concurrency from a new integration started this morning.
Jamie: CS pinged Coda — they deployed a batch import job hitting the inference API around 09:10 UTC.
ryan: Correlating: their spike started at 09:12 UTC. We see request rate ~6x baseline, tail tokens per request 6k-10k.
Anya: hypothesis: hotprefix + high concurrency => KV cache thrash -> repeated recomputation -> p99 spike.
Miguel: confirmed via logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:18Z] worker-12 WARN kv_cache.cpp: cache_eviction=high miss_ratio=0.82 req_seq=8123
[2026-03-14T09:12:19Z] worker-12 WARN runtime.cc: stall_detected streaming stalled for 1800ms
```
EngRuntime: Immediate mitigations we can do:
- route Coda to a larger instance pool (temporary)
- enable model-variant fallback to smaller-context variant
- apply per-customer concurrent request cap at the routing layer
- extend prefix cache TTL for pinned prefixes
ryan: I'm going to open an emergency routing rule. Applying a soft concurrent cap of 8 sessions for coda-prod-1 now.
ryan: `POST /admin/routing` payload:
```
{
  "customer": "coda",
  "concurrency_limit": 8,
  "policy": "queue"
}
```
deploy-bot: Deploy started for routing-rule-coda-2071112222 (job id 3452)
deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded in 34s
ryan: Cap is in. p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 1.1s within 90s. p95 unchanged.
Lina: CS told Coda to pause the import job and throttle their clients. They acknowledged and paused at 09:22 UTC.
Miguel: enabling prefix cache TTL bump for the hot prefixes used by their integration. Patching now.
EngRuntime: also switching their requests to model x-small-context variant to reduce KV pressure. Doing a gradual shift (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).
Anya: Observability notes: collect a sample of requests to add to an eval to detect long-prefix patterns automatically.
Jamie: customer impact: degraded latency for some sessions during 09:12-09:22 UTC, rate-limited for heavy import jobs after 09:22.
ryan: Severity: Sev3 (customer impact, mitigated by routing cap). Logging incident for postmortem.
Lina: I've drafted a message to the customer explaining root cause and remediation steps. Will share in #customer-success for approval.
Anya: Follow-ups:
- add automatic detection for single-tenant high-concurrency + long-prefix patterns
- document runbook steps to set concurrency caps and model fallback
- add unit tests for prefix cache eviction heuristics
Miguel: I'll schedule a capacity bump for coda-prod-1 for next week (temporary reserved pool) until they re-engineer the import.
ryan: Handing off to EngRuntime and CS for cleanup. Oncall remains until 09:45 UTC.
EngRuntime: taking postmortem action items. Thanks all.
Jamie: Coda accepted a short form post-incident report; will send draft by EOD.
incident-bot: Incident logged: INC-2071112222, severity=SEV3, owners=[ryan,EngRuntime,Anya]
ryan: Closing thread once follow-ups are created in JIRA. Good job everyone :thumbsup:
